conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: Currency symbol (equivalence of non-COBOL characters)
rows.adjudicator-notes: §12.3.7.3 SR20 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'any equivalence between that character and any other character in the computer's compile-time coded character set is defined by the implementor' -> OK §12.3.7.3 20)); A.1 cross-references SR21 where the equivalence is consumed. Code: DataBinder.Switches.cs:593 key = char.ToUpperInvariant(symbol), r21 collision COBOLNET0891; PictureAnalyzer.cs:139-155 matches picture characters by ToUpperInvariant. Probes /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s2/probe/: i43a.cob (2023) SYMBOL 'é', PIC É9.99 and é9.99 -> EUR1.50 / EUR2.50; i43b.cob 'é'->EUR plus 'É'->USD -> COBOLNET0891 at 2002/2023; i43d.cob full-width ｅ symbol with PIC Ｅ9.99 -> EUR1.50; i43e.cob bare CURRENCY SIGN 'é', PIC É9.99 / éé9.99 -> 'é1.50' / ' é2.50' identically at 85/2002/2014/2023; enum.cob (all code units 129..65535 through UPPER-CASE=ToUpperInvariant) -> only U+017F maps onto a picture letter (S). No golden pins the non-COBOL arm (l1_picture_currency_equivalent pins the COBOL-letter §8.1.3.2 arm), so Pinned by is '-' and the inventory row stays a GAP until one lands. Owning note: kb/Work PB1092 (open, documentation-only; this row discharges its item-43 half).
rows.rule-text: Currency symbol (equivalence of non-COBOL characters). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (12.3.7, SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, Syntax rule 21)

rows.subject: Currency symbol (implementor-defined prohibition of non-COBOL characters)
rows.adjudicator-notes: §8.1.2 (cite.py --check 8.1.2 'the implementor shall specify any such additional characters that are prohibited from use as a currency symbol' -> OK §8.1.2 3)). Code: DataBinder.Switches.cs ValidateCurrencyChar forbids char.IsAsciiDigit, char.ToUpperInvariant(c) in A B C D E N P R S V X Z, and ' ' + - , . * / ; ( ) \" =. Because the letter test goes through ToUpperInvariant, a non-COBOL character whose invariant uppercase is one of those letters is prohibited too; probe enum.cob (every code unit 129..65535 through UPPER-CASE, which is ToUpperInvariant) finds exactly one: U+017F. Probe i44.cob at 85/2023: 'ſ' -> COBOLNET0891; '€', '£', 'ｚ', 'Ω', 'ω' -> accepted and edit (2023: E=[€1.50] etc.); full-width digit '０' -> accepted, E=[０1.50]. The staged adjudication said 'the empty set' - corrected to {U+017F}. No golden pins it (Pinned by '-'). Owning note: kb/Work PB1397 (open, documentation-only; lists item 44).
rows.rule-text: Currency symbol (implementor-defined prohibition of non-COBOL characters). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.1.2, Computer's coded character set)

rows.subject: DEFINE directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.3.11.3 "Boolean-expression-1 shall be formed in accordance with 7.3.7" -> OK SR4. §7.3.7.2 SR1 (all operands boolean literals) enforced: n12 'B"1" B-AND 1' and s2 'B"1" B-AND "A"' -> COBOLNET1619; well-formed B-AND / B-OR evaluate (p1b, t6). No DEFINE-level test asserts the rejection (CompileTimeBooleanCceTests exercises the evaluator directly, not through >>DEFINE) - test-needed. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 - §7.3 compiler-directive facility; ISO/IEC 1989:2023 Annex E lists no change to §7.3.11 against 2014 (the 2002 introduction is not stated in the 2023 text itself; below 2002 the directive is COBOLNET0900)
rows.rule-text: Boolean-expression-1 shall be formed in accordance with 7.3.7, Compile-time boolean expressions.

rows.subject: DEFINE directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.3.11.4 "is unconditionally set to reference the value of the specified operand" -> OK GR3. AssignDefine skips the SR2 comparison when OVERRIDE and always stores the new value: q12 (1 -> 2 OVERRIDE -> 1 OVERRIDE, >>IF X = 1 selects), n5/q5 (2 OVERRIDE binds 2), r2 (PARAMETER OVERRIDE binds the env value 9). unit:ConditionalCompilationDefineTests.Redefine_WithOverride_Accepted asserts only the absence of COBOLNET1618, not the bound value - so it does not close the row. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 - §7.3 compiler-directive facility; ISO/IEC 1989:2023 Annex E lists no change to §7.3.11 against 2014 (the 2002 introduction is not stated in the 2023 text itself; below 2002 the directive is COBOLNET0900)
rows.rule-text: If the OVERRIDE phrase is specified, compilation-variable-name-1 is unconditionally set to reference the value of the specified operand.

rows.subject: DEFINE directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.3.11.4 "If literal-1 is specified, compilation-variable-name-1 references literal-1." -> OK GR8. Every literal category binds its literal: numeric (p1b N=3, F=1.5), alphanumeric (S="ABC"), national (u1 N"AB"), boolean (u1 B"10"), hexadecimal-alphanumeric (u1 X"41" = "A"); a floating-point literal is refused per §7.3.3 SR10 (n9). The numeric case is pinned by Define_SingleFractionLiteral_KeepsValue; no DEFINE test pins the non-numeric categories - test-needed. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 - §7.3 compiler-directive facility; ISO/IEC 1989:2023 Annex E lists no change to §7.3.11 against 2014 (the 2002 introduction is not stated in the 2023 text itself; below 2002 the directive is COBOLNET0900)
rows.rule-text: If literal-1 is specified, compilation-variable-name-1 references literal-1.

rows.subject: DISPLAY directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.3.12.4 "transferred in the sequence in which the operands are encountered" -> OK §7.3.12.4 4). Transfer order is vacuous under the GR2 no-listing disposition (nothing is transferred). Multi-operand syntax recognition belongs to PB807 (FMT). || editions (adjudicator): 2023 only (Foreword list of 2023 additions: 'Additional compiler directives were added: ... DISPLAY directive'); absent 1985/2002/2014
rows.rule-text: When a DISPLAY directive contains more than one operand the values of the operands are transferred in the sequence in which the operands are encountered.

rows.subject: DISPLAY directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.3.12.4 "the default is as if UPON LISTING were specified" -> OK §7.3.12.4 6). The default destination is the source listing, which this compiler does not produce; per GR2 the result is implementor-defined and is the documented recognize-and-consume (probe dd1). Vacuous under the disposition. || editions (adjudicator): 2023 only (Foreword list of 2023 additions: 'Additional compiler directives were added: ... DISPLAY directive'); absent 1985/2002/2014
rows.rule-text: If the UPON phrase is not specified, the default is as if UPON LISTING were specified.

rows.subject: Data-address-identifier
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR5 "This identifier format shall not be specified as a receiving operand" (cite.py OK 5)). Enforced by construction: addressIdentifier/dataAddressIdentifier appear only in sending slots (setAddressSender, CALL/INVOKE USING arguments - sending operands per §14.9.4.3 SR3/SR4 - and comparisonOperand); the SET Format 7 receiving `ADDRESS OF data-name-1` is the distinct setAddressReceiver rule (Annex D: not a data-address-identifier), screened by SR18. Probe N8 `MOVE P TO ADDRESS OF W` is refused (COBOLNET0901, reserved word ADDRESS) - rejected, though the message does not name SR5. No spec-derived negative test names SR5.
rows.rule-text: This identifier format shall not be specified as a receiving operand.

rows.subject: Dynamic-capacity tables
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 8.5.1.9.1 2) 'it may have an unlimited capacity' (--check OK 8.5.1.9.1 2)). The declaration imposes no ceiling: TO is only the EXPECTED capacity (exceedable, dyn_capacity_bounds SET 9 over TO 4 -> 9) and a TO-less table grows freely (probe p3 LZ(100000) -> LC=100000). The only ceiling is the implementor maximum MaxOccurrences = 0x3FFFFFFF, which 8.5.1.9.1 last paragraph expressly allows ('The actual limit for the current capacity imposed by the implementor and by current resource availability is referred to as the maximum capacity', --check OK). The resource-availability arm of that maximum is defective but belongs to GR-8.5.1.9.6-2 (raw OutOfMemory crash, see that record), not to this rule. No spec-derived golden asserts growth of a TO-less table to a large capacity, so test-ref is empty (test-needed). || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2014, 2023 (dynamic-capacity tables are a COBOL-2014 facility, ISO optional module A.4.4; absent from 1985/2002 - the compiler gates them COBOLNET0900 below 2014, probe p4 --std 2002; the 2023 Annex E records no change to 8.5.1.9)
rows.rule-text: it may have an unlimited capacity, and

rows.subject: ENTRY-CONVENTION clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 11.9.7.4 "When COBOL is specified, the naming convention and mapping of method-names and program-names are as specified in 8.3.2.2" -> OK GR2); §8.3.2.2 (cite.py --check 8.3.2.2 "the implementor defines the mapping between the user-defined word and the corresponding name" -> OK) leaves the word-to-externalized-name mapping implementor-defined; COBOL.NET's is case-insensitive (DOC-A.1-64). Both halves verified: program-names -- conformance:2014/pb232_entry_convention_cobol CALLs "w56ecin" to reach W56ECIN under ENTRY-CONVENTION IS COBOL (OUTER/INNER/OUTER-END); method-names -- probe p4 (class ECBASE with ENTRY-CONVENTION IS COBOL, METHOD-ID. SayHi, INVOKE O "sayhi" and "SAYHI" on INHERITS-derived ECDER) prints HI twice. test-ref deliberately EMPTY: the golden covers only the program-name half; the method-name half has no spec-derived test (test-needed). 'Other aspects implementor-defined' documented at DOC-A.1-64. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2014, 2023 (the 2023 Annex E lists no introduction or change of the clause, so it predates 2023; whether ISO 1989:2002 carried it is not derivable from specs/ISO_COBOL.md -- the code gates it 2014 as a recorded conservative choice, constructs.json options-entry-convention-2014) || Code sites (adjudicator, verbatim): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/OptionsBinder.cs#EntryConventionOf; ProgramTable.NameEquals (runtime case-insensitive name mapping, DOC-A.1-64)
rows.rule-text: When COBOL is specified, the naming convention and mapping of method-names and program-names are as specified in 8.3.2.2, User-defined words; other aspects of the entry convention are implementor-defined.

rows.subject: ENTRY-CONVENTION clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 11.9.7.4 a) "If a class definition includes the INHERITS clause, the entry convention is inherited from the first class specified", b) "If an interface definition includes the INHERITS clause, the entry convention is inherited from the first interface", c) "In all other cases, the entry convention is COBOL" -> all OK GR4). Every class/interface an INHERITS clause can name must be defined in the compilation group (COBOLNET0821 otherwise, measured with INHERITS FROM BASE) and every such element's convention is COBOL (other names refused COBOLNET2385), so the inherited convention in a) and b) is COBOL by construction; c) absent clause -> COBOL (OptionsModel null = COBOL). Verified: p4 (ECDER INHERITS FROM ECBASE, no clause) invokes the inherited method; p6 (interface ECIB INHERITS FROM ECIA) compiles/runs; consistent with §11.9.4 GR1 (cite OK). The golden pb232_entry_convention_cobol exercises only arm c) (contained W56ECIN with no clause); arms a)/b) untested -> test-ref empty. Correct vacuously while only COBOL exists; if an entry-convention-name is ever provided, the producer-only OptionsModel.EntryConvention (open PB298) must gain INHERITS inheritance. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2014, 2023 (the 2023 Annex E lists no introduction or change of the clause, so it predates 2023; whether ISO 1989:2002 carried it is not derivable from specs/ISO_COBOL.md -- the code gates it 2014 as a recorded conservative choice, constructs.json options-entry-convention-2014)
rows.rule-text: When ENTRY-CONVENTION is not specified, the entry convention used is as follows: a) If a class definition includes the INHERITS clause, the entry convention is inherited from the first class specified in the INHERITS clause. b) If an interface definition includes the INHERITS clause, the entry convention is inherited from the first interface specified in the INHERITS clause. c) In all other cases, the entry convention is COBOL.
